text: DALIO WARNS CHINA AND JAPAN COULD PULL BACK FROM TREASURIES Ray Dalio warns U.S. Treasuries are vulnerable to weakening demand from China and Japan, two of America’s largest foreign creditors. China’s holdings have fallen from $1.3 trillion in 2013 to about $618 billion, while Japan holds roughly $1.1 trillion. Dalio says reduced foreign demand could intensify pressure on U.S. borrowing as 10-year yields hover near 5.3%.

text: $TSLA - GOLDMAN: TESLA’S AI STORY MATTERS MORE THAN Q3 EARNINGS Goldman Sachs reiterated its Neutral rating and $360 price target on Tesla ahead of Q3 earnings. The bank expects improving vehicle revenue from the Model Y L ramp, but says higher costs and capex could limit 2026 EPS upside. Goldman believes robotaxis, FSD and humanoid robots will matter more for Tesla’s stock reaction than Q3 earnings themselves.

author: WalterBloomberg
text: JULIUS BAER SEES FINAL FED HIKE IN DECEMBER Julius Baer expects the Fed to deliver one final 25bp rate hike in December, followed by an extended pause. The bank points to a cooling U.S. labor market and sharply tighter financial conditions, driven more by rising long-term Treasury yields and a stronger dollar than by higher short-term rates. December is now seen as the most likely window for the final hike.

text: TRUMP SAYS U.S. WILL CONSIDER PERMANENT MILITARY BASE IN LITHUANIA President Trump says the U.S. will consider establishing a permanent military base in Lithuania, potentially replacing the current rotational model. Around 1,000 U.S. troops have typically rotated through Lithuania, which has hosted American forces since 2014.

text: UBS: TODAY’S TREASURY SELLOFF IS NOT 1999 ALL OVER AGAIN The 10-year Treasury yield recently hit 5.34%, reviving comparisons with 1999, when yields approached 5.8% during the dotcom boom. Iraq’s crude exports have averaged about 1.25 million barrels a day since March, far below the nearly 3.5 million barrels a day recorded last year. France’s 10-year yield rose to 4.91%, versus 3.61% for the 2-year, steepening the curve to roughly 130bp. Lescure said demand for 10-year debt remains solid, but 30-year issuance is “a bit trickier” amid fiscal and political concerns.
